cases.why: AWS publishes this exact key id in its own documentation as the example value; it authenticates nothing. The `AKIA` type prefix is what makes the rule high-precision without a checksum. Stored assembled (ADR 0010): the file never carries the contiguous key literal, the loader rebuilds it, and the detector runs on the real format.

cases.content_template: Identifiant temporaire {token} dans la trace du job.
cases.why: `ASIA` is the temporary session-credential prefix; the body is placeholder text. The rule must cover the whole assigned prefix family, not only `AKIA`. An AWS key id is exactly twenty characters — this case was first written with a seventeen-character body and the detector correctly refused it, which is the length bound doing its job.

The `A3T…` prefix family: absent from AWS's documented unique-id prefix page, present in AWS's own git-secrets pattern and in gitleaks' rule. The head-to-head drew a catalogue instance starting `A3TR` and the rule, listing only the documented prefixes, missed it (ADR 0030); this case is that miss made permanent (ADR 0030 Am. 1). Placeholder body in the base32 alphabet a real key id uses; twenty characters exactly. Assembled per ADR 0010.
The `sk-proj-` shape with an obviously placeholder body. Never a live key. Assembled per ADR 0010.
The older `sk-` shape, placeholder body. Assembled per ADR 0010.

cases.content_template: Jeton OAuth {token} exposé dans la réponse.
cases.why: The OAuth variant. The rule covers the whole `gh[pousr]_` family, because a token leaks the same whichever letter it carries. Assembled per ADR 0010.

cases.content_template: The fine-grained token {token} was pasted into the issue.
cases.why: GitHub's fine-grained personal access token: `github_pat_` + 82 word characters, the shape GitHub publishes. The `gh[pousr]_` rule did not cover it and the head-to-head said so (ADR 0030); closed under ADR 0030 Am. 1. Placeholder body, split where GitHub's real tokens carry an underscore after their 22nd character. Assembled per ADR 0010.

cases.content_template: Billing is configured with {token} right now.
cases.why: Stripe secret key shape with a placeholder body. Stored assembled (ADR 0010): the live-key format is one a host secret scanner push-protects (GitHub blocked exactly this literal), so the file carries fragments the loader joins, never the contiguous key.

A restricted TEST key. Detected on purpose: a credential leaving in a tool result is a credential leaving, and 'it was only the test key' is a decision for the operator, not the detector. Assembled per ADR 0010.

cases.content_template: Maps key {token} appeared in the log.
cases.why: Google API key shape (`AIza` + 35), placeholder body. Assembled per ADR 0010.

cases.content_template: Bot token {token} was posted to the channel.
cases.why: Slack BOT token, at the grammar Slack issues: `xoxb-` then two numeric ids then a 24-character body. The previous vector was `xoxb-EXAMPLE-ONLY-SYNTHETIC-NOT-A-REAL-TOKEN`, which has no Slack token shape at all — letters where the ids are digits — and the rule had been loosened until it matched it, at a measured cost of 14 external false positives (ADR 0021 Am. 2). Synthetic under ADR 0009 and format-faithful: checked to match gitleaks' own `slack-bot-token` pattern, which is an external definition rather than this repository's. Assembled per ADR 0010.

cases.why: Slack USER token: `xoxp-` then three numeric ids then a 28-34 character body. Replaces `xoxp-EXAMPLE-ONLY-SYNTHETIC-USER-TOKEN`, same reason as the bot vector. Checked against gitleaks' own `slack-user-token` pattern.

cases.why: PEM armour around a body that base64-decodes to the words 'EXAMPLE ONLY - not a key - synthetic'. No key material exists. The whole BLOCK is the value to locate: a finding that spanned only the BEGIN line would be masked to exactly that and would forward the body underneath it. Kept as a literal: a PEM block over placeholder text is a documentation value no host scanner push-protects.

Clé tronquée dans la réponse :
-----BEGIN EC PRIVATE KEY-----
UExBQ0VIT0xERVIgLSBzeW50aGV0aWMgLSBub3QgYSBrZXk=
cases.why: A truncated block with no END line — what a streamed or clipped tool result actually looks like. The rule swallows to the end of the content rather than matching nothing: masking too much beats forwarding a partial key.

The self-signed token every JWT tutorial publishes, over fictional claims. The header decodes to {"alg":"HS256","typ":"JWT"} — which is the entire claim, since the three-segment shape is shared with file names and version strings.
An `alg: none` token — unsigned, and exactly the kind worth catching on the way out. The validator keys on the header being a JSON object declaring `alg`, not on the algorithm being a real one.

The ~/.aws/credentials file, the carrier AWS's own documentation shows. The value is AWS's published documentation secret — the exact string git-secrets (awslabs) ships in its allowlist, verified at source 2026-08-31 — so it authenticates nothing (ADR 0009). Stored assembled (ADR 0010). The canonical case of the category: the forty-character base64 body carries no vendor prefix, so the name it is assigned to is the entire discriminant (ADR 0022).

An STS AssumeRole response fragment. The field is CamelCase SecretAccessKey with no 'aws' anywhere in reach — the keyword set must know AWS's own response vocabulary, not only the env-var spelling. The value is AWS's second published documentation secret (ADR 0009).

cases.why: French support-ticket prose carrying the raw credentials line — the leak shape a banking support agent actually produces. The identifier stays English inside French prose, which is what the keyword set banks on.
A German-commented deployment YAML. The colon is in the vendor grammar's operator set, and the identifier stays English in de code — the reason the keywords are AWS vocabulary, not translations.

Terraform's provider block: the adjacent keyword is bare secret_key, and 'aws' sits on another line, out of any single-line grammar's reach. The case that forces the third keyword alternative — measured at zero false-positive cost on every population (ADR 0022).
